questions.q: If the length of the minor axis of an ellipse is equal to one fourth of the distance between the foci, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & 2 \mathrm{~b}=\frac{1}{4}(2 \mathrm{ae}) \\ & \frac{\mathrm{b}}{\mathrm{a}}=\frac{\mathrm{e}}{4} \\ & \mathrm{e}=\sqrt{1-\frac{\mathrm{b}^2}{\mathrm{a}^2}} \\ & \mathrm{e}=\sqrt{1-\frac{\mathrm{e}^2}{16}} \\ & \mathrm{e}^2\left(1+\frac{1}{16}\right)=1 \\ & \mathrm{e}=\frac{4}{\sqrt{17}}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: In an ellipse, with centre at the origin, if the difference of the lengths of major axis and minor axis is 10 and one of the foci is at \left(0,5\sqrt{3}\right),$ then the length of its latus rectum is:$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given, difference of the lengths of major and minor axis is $10$.
$⇒ 2b - 2a = 10$ … (1)
One of the focii is \left(0, 5\sqrt{3}\right)$
$⇒ be = 5\sqrt{3}$ … (2)
Also $a^{2} = b^{2} \left(1 - e^{2}\right)$ .......(3)
$⇒ a^{2} = b^{2} - 75$
$⇒ \left(b - a\right)\left($a + b\right) = 75$
$⇒ a + b = 15$ … (4)
From (1) and (4)
$a = 5$ and $b = 10$
Hence length of the latus rectum $= \dfrac{2a^{2}}{b} =2 ⋅ \dfrac{25}{10} =5$

questions.q: If the ellipse $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$~meets the line $\dfrac{x}{7} + \dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{6}} = 1$~on the $x$-axis and the line $\dfrac{x}{7} - \dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{6}} = 1$~on the $y$-axis, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$~meets the line~$\dfrac{x}{7} + \dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{6}} = 1$~on the~$x$-axis, so at~$x -$axis~$y = 0$~putting in both equation and comparing we get,~$a = 7$~

And~$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$~meets the line~$\dfrac{x}{7} - \dfrac{y}{2\sqrt{6}} = 1$~on the~$y$-axis where~$x = 0$~so putting in both equation and comparing we get,~$b = 2\sqrt{6}$

Therefore,~$e^{2} = 1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2} = 1 - \dfrac{24}{49}$

$⇒ e = \sqrt{\dfrac{25}{49}} = \dfrac{5}{7}$

questions.q: Let the product of the focal distances of the point  \left(\sqrt{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right)$ on the ellipse $\frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1,(\mathrm{a}\gt\mathrm{b})$, be $\frac{7}{4}$. Then the absolute difference of the eccentricities of two such ellipses is$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Product of focal distances }=\left(a+e x_1\right)\left(a-e x_1\right) \\ & =a^2-e^2 x_1^2=a^2-e^2(3) \\ & =a^2-3 e^2=\frac{7}{4} \Rightarrow a^2=\frac{7}{4}+3 e^2 \\ & \Rightarrow 4 a^2=7+12 e^2 \\ & &\left(\sqrt{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right) \text { lines on } \frac{x^2}{a^2}+\frac{y^2}{b^2}=1 \\ & \therefore \frac{3}{a^2}+\frac{1}{4 b^2}=1\end{aligned}$\begin{aligned} & \frac{3}{\mathrm{a}^2}+\frac{1}{4\left(\mathrm{a}^2\right)\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right)}=1 \\ & 12\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right)+1=4 \mathrm{a}^2\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right) \\ & 13-12 \mathrm{e}^2=\left(7+12 \mathrm{e}^2\right)\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right) \\ & \Rightarrow 13-12 \mathrm{e}^2=7-7 \mathrm{e}^2+12 \mathrm{e}^2-12 \mathrm{e}^4 \\ & \Rightarrow 12 \mathrm{e}^4-17 \mathrm{e}^2+6=0 \\ & \therefore \mathrm{e}^2=\frac{17 \pm \sqrt{289-288}}{24}=\frac{17 \pm 1}{24}=\frac{3}{4} & \frac{2}{3} \\ & \therefore \mathrm{e}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} & \sqrt{\frac{2}{3}} \\ & \therefore \text { difference }==\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}-\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}=\frac{3-2 \sqrt{2}}{2 \sqrt{3}}\end{aligned}$$

questions.q: Let $S = \left\{\left(x, y\right) \in R^{2}: \dfrac{y2}{1 + r} - \dfrac{x2}{1 - r} = 1\right\},$ where $r \ne \pm 1 .$ Then $S$ represents:
options: An ellipse whose eccentricity is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{r + 1}},$ when $r > 1 .$
A hyperbola whose eccentricity is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{r + 1}},$ when $0 < r < 1 .$
An ellipse whose eccentricity is $\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{r + 1}},$ when $r > 1$
A hyperbola whose eccentricity is $\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1 - r}},$ when $0 < r < 1$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& $\dfrac{y^{2}}{1 + r} - \dfrac{x^{2}}{1 - r} = 1$

If $r \in \left(0, 1\right)$ then this curve is a hyperbola whose eccentricity is \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{1 - r}{1 + r}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{r + 1}}.~

If $r > 1$ , then this curve is an ellipse whose
eccentricity is $\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{r - 1}{r + 1}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{r + 1}}.& $

questions.q: Let the eccentricity of an ellipse $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1, a > b$, be $\dfrac{1}{4}$. If this ellipse passes through the point  \left(- 4\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}, 3\right)$, then $a^{2} + b^{2}$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given,

$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1a > b$

Now using~eccentricity~formula,~$e^{2} = 1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}$

We get,~$\dfrac{1}{16} = 1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{b2}{a2} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{16} = \dfrac{15}{16} ⇒ b^{2} = \dfrac{15}{16}a^{2}$

Now again~$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$~is passing through~ \left(- 4\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}, 3\right)$~on satisfying the point we get,

$⇒ \dfrac{16 \times \dfrac{2}{5}}{a2} + \dfrac{9}{b2} = 1$

$⇒ \dfrac{32}{5a^{2}} + \dfrac{9}{b2} = 1$

Now putting the value~$b^{2} = \dfrac{15}{16}a^{2}$~in above equation we get,

$\dfrac{32}{5a^{2}} + \dfrac{9}{\dfrac{15}{16}a^{2}} = 1$

$\dfrac{80}{5a^{2}} = 1$

$16 = a^{2}$

So,~$b^{2} = 15$~and~$a^{2} + b^{2} = 15 + 16 = 31$

$

questions.q: Let an ellipse $E: \dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1, a^{2} > b^{2}$, passes through  \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}, 1\right)$ and has eccentricity $\dfrac{1}{3}$. If a circle, centered at focus $F ( \alpha, 0 ) , \alpha > 0$, of $E$ and radius $\dfrac{2}{3}$, intersects $E$ at two points $P$ and $Q$, then $PQ^{2}$ is equal to :$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The ellipse& $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$~passes through the point~ \left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{2}}, 1\right)$

So,~$\dfrac{3}{2a^{2}} + \dfrac{1}{b2} = 1 . . . \left(1\right)$ and $1 - $\dfrac{b2}{a2} = \dfrac{1}{3} . . . \left(2\right)$

On solving equations~ \left(1\right)$~and~ \left(2\right)$, we get

$⇒ a^{2} = 3 & b^{2} = 2$

$⇒ $\dfrac{x2}{3} + \dfrac{y2}{2} =$1 . . . \left(3\right)$

We know that, focii of the ellipse~$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} =1$~is~ \left(\pmae, 0\right)$

Here,~$a = \sqrt{3} \text{ and } e = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$∴$~Its focus is~ \left($1, 0\right) \left($∵ $\alpha$> 0\right)$

Now, equation of circle is

$( x - 1{)}^{2} + y^{2} = $\dfrac{4}{3} . . . \left($4\right)$

Solving \left($3\right)$~and \left(4\right)$ we get

$y = \pm \dfrac{2}{3},x = 1$

$⇒ PQ^{2} = \sqrt{ \left(1 - 1\right)2 + \left(\dfrac{2}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3})2}$

$= \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\right)2 = \dfrac{16}{3}$

$

questions.q: Let& $PQ$ be a focal chord of the parabola $y^{2} = 4x$~such that it subtends an angle of $\dfrac{π}{2}$~at the point  \left(3, 0\right)$. Let the line segment~$PQ$ be also a focal chord of the ellipse $E: \dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1, a^{2} > b^{2}$. If $e$~is the eccentricity of the ellipse $E$, then the value of $\dfrac{1}{e2}$& is equal to$
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
$Since& $PQ$~is focal chord of the parabola~$y^{2} = 4ax$

so let~$P \left(t^{2}, 2t\right)$,~$Q \left(\dfrac{1}{t2}, - \dfrac{2}{t}\right)$~and~$R \left(3, 0\right)$

Given~${m}_{PR} \cdot {m}_{PQ} = -1$

\dfrac{2t}{t^{2} - 3} \times \dfrac{- \dfrac{2}{t}}{\dfrac{1}{t2} - 3} = -$1$

\left(t^{2} - 1\right)2 = 0$

$⇒ t = 1$

i.e.~$PQ$~must be the~latus rectum

We get~$P \left($1, 2\right) \text{ and } Q \left($1, - 2\right)$

For ellipse

\dfrac{2b^{2}}{a} =$4 & ae = 1$

Also~$b^{2} = a^{2} \left($1 - e^{2}\right)$

$∴ a = 1 + $\sqrt{2}

and$e^{2} = 3 - $2\sqrt{2}

Hence~\dfrac{1}{e2} = \dfrac{1}{3 - 2\sqrt{2}} =$3 + $2\sqrt{2}

$

questions.q: Let ${E}_{1}: \dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1, a > b .$~Let ${E}_{2}$ be another ellipse such that it touches the end points of major axis of ${E}_{1}$ and the foci of ${E}_{2}$ are the end points of minor axis of ${E}_{1} .$~If ${E}_{1}$ and ${E}_{2}$ have same eccentricities, then its value is:
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Given& ellipse is& ${E}_{1}: \dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1, a > b$~and~${E}_{2}$~is another ellipse which touches the end points of the major axis~of~${E}_{1}$~and foci of~${E}_{2}$~are at the minor axis of~${E}_{1},$~thus the two ellipses are given by the following diagram.

Since, the ellipse~${E}_{2}$~touches the major axis of the ellipse ${E}_{1}$, hence, the minor axis of the ellipse~${E}_{2}$~is~${a}_{1} = a .$

Now, let the major axis of the ellipse~${E}_{2}$~is~${b}_{1} = c$~and it is obvious from the diagram and the given conditions that~${b}_{1} > {a}_{1} .$

We know that the eccentricity of an ellipse~$\dfrac{x2}{A2} + \dfrac{y2}{B2} = 1, A > B$~is~$\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{B2}{A2}} .$

Thus, for the ellipse~${E}_{1},$~we have~$e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}}$~and for the ellipse~${E}_{2},$~we have~${e}_{1} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{a2}{c2}} .$

Given,~$e = {e}_{1}$

$\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}} = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{a2}{c2}}$

$⇒ 1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2} = 1 - \dfrac{a2}{c2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{b2}{a2} = \dfrac{a2}{c2}$

$⇒ c^{2} = \dfrac{a4}{b2}$

$⇒ c = \dfrac{a2}{b} . . . \left(i\right)$

Also, given that the foci of~${E}_{2}$~are the end points of the minor axis of~${E}_{1},$~thus~$b = ce$

$⇒ c = $\dfrac{b}{e} . . . \left(ii\right)$

From the above two equations, we get~\dfrac{b}{e} = \dfrac{a2}{b}

$⇒ e = $\dfrac{b2}{a2}

Now, using the definition of eccentricity, we get~$e = $\dfrac{b2}{a2} =$1 - e^{2}$

$⇒ e^{2} + e - 1 = 0$

Now, applying the Sridharacharya's formula for the roots of a quadratic equation, i.e. if~$ax^{2} + bx + c = 0, a \ne 0,$~then~$x = $\dfrac{- b \pm \sqrt{b^{2} - 4ac}}{2a},~we get

$e = $\dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{{1}^{2} - 4 \times 1 \times \left(- 1\right)}}{2 \times 1}

$⇒ e = $\dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{1 + 4}}{2}

$⇒ e = $\dfrac{- 1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{2}

But, eccentricity can never be negative, hence~$e = $\dfrac{- 1 + \sqrt{5}}{2} .

$

questions.q: If the length of the minor axis of ellipse is equal to half of the distance between the foci, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
The length of minor axis is given by \left(2b\right)$ and the distance between foci is given by \left(2ae\right)$

Given: $2b = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2ae$

$⇒ 2b = ae$

$⇒ 4b^{2} = a^{2}e^{2}$

$⇒ \dfrac{4b^{2}}{a2} = e^{2}$

$⇒ 4\left(1 - e^{2}\right) = e^{2}$

$⇒ 4 - 4e^{2} = e^{2}$

$⇒ e = \dfrac{2}{5}$

questions.q: Let& $S$~and~$S^{'}$ be the foci of an ellipse and~$B$~be any one of the extremities of its minor axis. If $\Delta S^{'}BS$ is a right angled triangle with right angle at~$B$~and area \left(\Delta S^{'}BS\right) = 8sq . units$, then the length of a latus rectum of the ellipse is :$

Given that,&

$∠SBS^{'} = \dfrac{π}{2}$

$⇒ ∠OBS = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Also, area \left(∆ SBS^{'}\right) = 8$~

Area of $\triangle P Q R$
$\begin{aligned}
& =\frac{1}{2}(2 a)(a \sin \theta+b) \\ & \therefore \text { maximum area }=a(a+b) \\ & \quad=4(4+2 \sqrt{3})=8(2+\sqrt{3})
